overall_summary: The channel is experiencing its strongest performance when focusing on extreme space anomalies, particularly exoplanets with bizarre environmental characteristics (e.g., TrES-2b, burning ice, supersonic rubies). Conversely, psychology and brain-related facts are severely underperforming, especially when repeated or re-uploaded with minor title variations.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,016 views, 36 likes), 'The Planet of Burning Ice...' (1,055 views, 8 likes), and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (721 views, 25 likes) are the channel's top-performing videos.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on highly visual, extreme planetary conditions and space mysteries. Keep video durations for this category around 21 seconds to allow for detailed visual storytelling.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'What Does Outer Space Actually Smell Like?' (368 views) and 'The Planet Where It Rains Molten Iron!' (349 views) leverage sensory-driven curiosity (smell, touch, extreme temperature) to drive clicks.
winning_patterns.action: Structure hooks around sensory contradictions (e.g., tasting, smelling, or hearing things in space or extreme environments).

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' struggled across multiple attempts (ranging from 5 to 53 views), and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' generated only 17 views.
weak_patterns.action: Pause the production of basic cognitive psychology facts. If psychology is revisited, frame it through a historical mystery or a high-stakes survival scenario rather than a generic text-on-screen fact.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'This Star Is Older Than the Universe!' generated only 11 views, showing that purely temporal or abstract space concepts lack the immediate visual hook of physical planetary environments.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid abstract astrophysics theories unless they can be tied directly to a tangible, highly visual object or a 'what-if' physical scenario.

next_video.concept: The planet where the oceans are made of boiling lava and it rains solid rock.
next_video.opening_direction: Start with a high-contrast visual of a spacecraft melting: 'There is a planet in our galaxy where the oceans are literally made of boiling, liquid rock...'
next_video.twist_direction: ...but the real nightmare is the weather. Because the lava evaporates, it condenses in the atmosphere and rains solid stones back down to the surface.
next_video.reason: Aligns perfectly with the 21-second duration of our top-performing exoplanet videos and leverages the proven 'extreme weather/bizarre planet' formula that generated our highest view and engagement spikes.

experiment: Test a 21-second Short on a cinematic animal survival story (e.g., 'The Only Animal That Can Survive a Volcanic Eruption') to see if the high-retention 'survival' storytelling format can replicate the success of the extreme space videos.
